findings.text: the drain predicate matches only the leading '+' token of the scheduler's State= value, so it fires only where the drain token leads; measured over 422 live nodes it fires on 0 of the 82 that carry a DRAIN token, all of which carry it as a flag after the base state (MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED 43, ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED 39). Positive control fires on DRAIN, DRAINED, DRAINING and DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING; 0 false positives on the 340 healthy nodes. This is the only warning that can fire for the unbounded hold, which the run's own record states.

the record states the flag direction as fact ('flags are reported after a + (DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING) ... the leading token is what decides whether the node is going out of service') and generalises to 'a draining or drained node warns on its own', while the live scheduler here reports base-first; the fixture that certifies it (tests/agent/test_fleet.py:240, node_state='DRAINING') was written in the code's own idiom, so the passing suite cannot show the miss.

the record quotes the declared mutation as a paraphrase ('account=site.fleet_account -> account=site.account in the fleet status job lookup') where the declared text is 'revert the fleet status lookup to filter the queue by site.account instead of the fleet account; the test asserting the account operand in the squeue argv must then be observed to fail'; the log's first line is byte-identical to the declared text (185 bytes, compared equal), so the receipt is authentic and only the prose that quotes it differs.

the two guard branches inside _fleet_node_state - the not-a-node-name return at :1264 and the failed-query return at :1272 - are unexecuted by the focused suite, whose only fake returns returncode 0 for a clean node name, so the record's 'unknown reads as unknown and is not warned about' rests on inspection; coverage of imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py is 95% with 123, 154, 159 and 186 unexecuted.

Review of run r-20260921T085932378383-fleet-status-sees-the-allocation, plan imas-ambix:slurm-hosted-agent-fleet section 7 (step six, 'give the allocation a visible lifetime'). Landed change: 5b6f84e7 (the charged-account operand, the scontrol node read, parse_node_state, node_is_draining, the drain warning and eight test changes), 7a8eb5bb (the landing record and the plan comment). Base 0dcf297d0fd0b2019cad02f1d4ec64bb9f960acc, head 7a8eb5bb23d8cb5436f3f6eff07a83daf740582f. Read for this review: the reviewed run's manifest, prompt, negative-control log and resume advice; the five reviewed sources at the reviewed blobs; the plan's section 5 and section 7 and its landing comment; and five probes run here - the focused suite and the whole-tree lint at the reviewed revision, the wider consumer suite on an all_debug node, the declared mutation re-applied in a scratch export of the reviewed sha, a boundary mutation against the replacement assertion, and a census of the reviewed drain predicate over every live node's real State= string.

VERDICT goal: the goal is a status surface that reads the allocation the hold generator actually charges the job to and warns the operator before the control group is torn down. The account half is correct and verified end to end through the code; the warning half is delivered for spellings this scheduler does not emit, so on the fleet's own partition it does not fire.

VERDICT done_when: eight clauses. Measured here - (1) the account repair holds (generator --account=iter, command -A iter, equal; the alternative account grpa differs, so the probe can see a mismatch); (2) the account operand is asserted in the faked runner's argv and that assertion is the one that goes red under the re-applied mutation; (3) the drain warning is implemented but fires on 0 of the 82 live nodes that carry a DRAIN token, because the scheduler reports the base state first; (4) the tautology is replaced by a property with measured discriminating power; (5) the declared mutation's first line is byte-identical to the declared text and reproduces independently at the named id; (6) both gates re-run exit 0; (7) no SLURM job was touched, consistent with the queue read here; (8) both label sweeps are empty - so clause (3) is the clause that does not hold.

VERDICT write_paths: the declared paths are the five in the run manifest; git diff --stat 0dcf297d..7a8eb5bb shows 302 insertions and 16 deletions across exactly those five and no file outside them, the reviewed worktree is clean at head, and the plan's plan-version and plan-modified meta lines are not touched by the diff.

VERDICT manifest: cross-checked line by line. Commits, gate commands and summaries match their logs; the negative-control log is complete (declared line verbatim, applied edit, red at the named id, restore, green); follow-on (3) correctly reports that the plan and evidence edits were made by hand. One overstatement: the artifacts line and the landed record describe the drain warning as covering 'drain, drain/draining' spellings generally, where the measured coverage is drain-leading spellings only.

VERDICT diff: read commit by commit against the base. 5b6f84e7 is additive and coherent - the account operand, the node-state read and parse, the warning line, and tests that assert the argv operand and derive the threshold fixtures from the constant. 7a8eb5bb records the landing without touching plan meta. Both commit messages carry real bodies and no trailer.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 13
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the account defect is real and the repair is correct - fleet.py:50 charges the hold with account=site.fleet_account, slurm.py:72 renders '#SBATCH --account=', profile.py:483 defaults it to 'iter', and cli.py:335 feeds the same value into the lookup that emits '-A', measured here as '#SBATCH --account=iter' against 'squeue -h -u mcintos -A iter' with grpa as the differing control. Docked because the second half of the goal - advance notice before the control group is torn down - is delivered as a predicate that fires on 0 of the 82 nodes on this cluster whose scheduler reports a drain, so the one warning that can fire for the hold (the wall clock cannot, being unbounded) is silent in the case it exists for.

SCORE evidence: 11
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the receipts taken are strong and re-verified here - the mutation receipt is byte-identical (185 bytes) and reproduces independently, both gates exit 0 with their summary lines quoted, the wider consumer reads 198 passed on all_debug (the target ran test_agent.py alone, 192), and the new account test reads the argv operand rather than the printed sentence. Docked because the drain evidence is a fixture written in the implementation's own idiom (node_state='DRAINING' at test_fleet.py:240) and the record generalises it to 'draining or drained' without one reading of a live node state, so the suite that passes cannot show the miss. The population that could have falsified it was available at no cost: a single scontrol reading answers it.

SCORE scope_discipline: 18
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: exactly the five declared paths with 302 insertions across two conventional commits carrying real bodies, no AI attribution in either message (line-anchored), no plan label, ticket or version suffix in any added line (both sweeps empty), and no plan meta line touched - the hand-edit stayed inside the prose it owned. Docked nothing material; the one thing a reader must know is that the plan and evidence edits bypassed the reckon writer, which the run's own manifest already states.

SCORE durability: 12
JUSTIFICATION durability: the account guard is durable and was shown to fire - re-applying the declared mutation turns the suite red at the named test, so a regression to the site-account filter is caught by the suite. The drain guard is the opposite shape: committed, tested and green, while blind to the spelling this cluster emits, so nothing in the suite observes the failure and a regression cannot be caught by it either. Measured coverage of imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py is 95% with 123, 154, 159 and 186 unexecuted, and two guard branches inside _fleet_node_state (cli.py:1264, cli.py:1272) are not exercised.

SCORE fit: 14
JUSTIFICATION fit: the repair follows the module's idiom closely - a keyword-only operand whose default reproduces the previous expression exactly, the node read as a small function beside the lookup it serves, one warning appended in the existing describe_* style, docstrings updated to state the new behaviour, and a test that asserts an operand rather than a rendering. Docked because the drain predicate does not follow the grammar of the value it parses: a scheduler State= is a base state joined with '+' flags, and reading only the leading token happens to work for the spellings in the fixtures and not for the scheduler's.

FINDING imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py:138 the drain predicate reads only the leading '+' token of the scheduler's State= value and prefix-matches DRAIN against it, so it fires only where the drain token leads. Measured over the live cluster: 842 sinfo node lines / 422 unique nodes; 'scontrol show node' State= read for all 422; 82 carry a DRAIN token and all 82 carry it as a flag AFTER the base state - MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED (43 nodes) and ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED (39). The reviewed predicate fires on 0 of the 82. The positive control in the same run fires on DRAIN, DRAINED, DRAINING and DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING, so the zero is a property of the spellings rather than a dead instrument; the 340 nodes with no DRAIN token produce 0 false positives, so the direction of the error is a silent miss, not a spurious warning. This is the case the node added the warning for: the hold is unbounded by construction, so no wall-clock threshold can fire for it, and the record itself says so. The fleet's partition rigel held 0 draining nodes at this reading (7 alloc, 52 idle, 1 maint), so the miss is not live on the fleet's own node today - it is one scontrol update away and it was measured on 82 nodes of the same cluster.

FINDING docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html:777 the record's drain evidence rests on a spelling this cluster does not emit, and the direction is stated as fact: 'Flags are reported after a + (DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING) and are dropped, because the leading token is what decides whether the node is going out of service' is true of the fixtures and false of the live scheduler here, where the leading token is the base state and DRAIN is the flag. The same generalisation reaches the run manifest, which records 'a draining node warns on its own' without a reading from a live node. The consequence for a reader is the shape this plan's earlier node hit at the wall clock: the record reports a coverage the instrument does not have, and the fixture that certifies it was written in the code's own idiom.

FINDING docs/evidence/archive/slurm-hosted-agent-fleet-landed.html:812 the record quotes the declared mutation as 'account=site.fleet_account -> account=site.account in the fleet status job lookup', which is a paraphrase: the declared text is 'revert the fleet status lookup to filter the queue by site.account instead of the fleet account; the test asserting the account operand in the squeue argv must then be observed to fail'. The log's first line is byte-identical to the declared text (185 bytes, compared equal here), so the receipt is authentic - the gap is only in the prose that quotes it, and the run's own manifest already flags it as a follow-on.

ANSWER (a) whether the account the status lookup queries is the account the generator charges the job to: YES, checked through the code rather than from the message. imas_ambix/agent/fleet.py:50 passes account=site.fleet_account into slurm's header emitter, imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:72 renders that as '#SBATCH --account={account}', and imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:483 fixes fleet_account at 'iter' (env AMBIX_AGENT_FLEET_ACCOUNT, line 547), while cli.py:335 passes site.fleet_account into the lookup whose argv carries it at cli.py:1222 as '-A'. Measured: the generated script reads '#SBATCH --account=iter' and the command's argv reads 'squeue -h -u mcintos -A iter -o %i|%j|%T|%M|%R|%b|%k|%L' - equal, and the control that the two candidate accounts differ (site.account='grpa', site.fleet_account='iter') shows the comparison is not vacuous. The defect stated in the dispatch reproduces independently: with the lookup restored to the site account the account assertion goes red with 'assert grpa == iter'.

ANSWER (b) whether widening _running_jobs with an optional account parameter changed behaviour for ANY existing caller: NO. Enumerated by AST at the reviewed revision: ten production call sites in two modules, 'account' is keyword-only (added after the '*' marker, so no positional argument can bind it), and the default is None which reaches 'account if account is not None else site.account' - the base expression, character for character. The callers and their resolved account: cli.py:335 fleet_status -> site.fleet_account ('iter'), the only caller that passes it; cli.py:656 status -> site.account; cli.py:917 and :926 _resolve_log_job -> site.account; cli.py:1151 _republish_endpoint_document -> site.account; cli.py:1398 _running_ambix_job_on_port -> site.account; cli.py:1451 _discover_live_routes -> site.account; cli.py:1515 _resolve_router_upstreams -> site.account; registry.py:564 and :575 main -> site.account. Measured at the seam: default and job_ids calls emit '-A grpa', the fleet status call emits '-A iter'. The wider consumer suite on an all_debug node (tests/test_agent.py + tests/test_agent_router_resolution.py) reads 198 passed, and no test outside tests/agent/test_fleet.py invokes 'agent fleet status', so the positional-only fakes elsewhere cannot be reached by the new keyword.

ANSWER (c) whether the drain detection matches every spelling the scheduler can report, including the plus-separated flag forms, and whether it can raise a false warning on a healthy node: NO, and NO. Not every spelling: over 422 live nodes the predicate fires on 0 of the 82 that carry a DRAIN token, because every one of those 82 carries it after the base state (MIXED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED 43, ALLOCATED+DRAIN+REBOOT_REQUESTED 39) and the parser keeps only the leading token (fleet.py:138) before prefix-matching (fleet.py:145). The positive control fires on DRAIN, DRAINED, DRAINING and DRAINING+NOT_RESPONDING, so the instrument is alive and the miss is the base-first ordering. No false warning on a healthy node: 0 of the 340 non-draining nodes flag, and no healthy spelling observed leads with DRAIN, so the error is one-directional. Scope: rigel, the fleet's own partition, held no draining node at the reading, so this is a latent miss rather than a live one on the fleet's node today.

ANSWER (d) whether the replacement threshold assertion tests a property or has merely moved the literal: a PROPERTY. The literal is gone - 'assert REMAINING_WARNING_SECONDS == 1800' is removed from test_fleet_status_warns_inside_the_threshold and no 1800 remains anywhere in the file - and the replacement derives both fixtures from the constant sixty seconds either side, so it asserts the boundary behaviour rather than restating a value. Measured discriminating power: in a scratch export of the reviewed sha, decoupling the boundary from the constant ('seconds < REMAINING_WARNING_SECONDS' -> 'seconds < 600') turns two tests red (the new boundary test and the pre-existing inside-threshold test, whose 29m fixture stops warning), while the assertion the node removed still evaluates REMAINING_WARNING_SECONDS == 1800 -> True under that mutation, so the old form could not have failed on it. Residual, minor and not the defect that was replaced: the exact equality point (seconds == the threshold) is not exercised, so '<' and '<=' are not distinguished.

Note for the next reader: the census instrument was corrected once before it was trusted - the first run derived its ground truth from the same parsed token the predicate sees and reported zero draining nodes against a cluster holding 164 draining sinfo entries, which is why the recorded run extracts the raw State= value independently and runs a positive control first. This review wrote nothing inside the repository; its probe scripts and logs are the artifacts of run r-20260921T092818355609-review-of-fleet-status-sees-the-allocation.
